## 3. The evidence that moved it

**Nature reports glioma cells recruiting the brain's own machinery for adaptive plasticity ([37914930](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37914930/)).** This is the strongest form the `neuro-immune-microbiome-axis` claim can take. The weak version says nerves modulate tumours; the strong version says the two are running one mechanism, and a tumour that co-opts synaptic plasticity — the process by which the host circuit learns — is not being modulated by the nervous system, it is participating in it. A tumour with a stake in circuit remodelling is also a tumour whose growth is coupled to what the patient's brain is doing, which is a different therapeutic object from a mass with nerves nearby.

**Three groups reach tumour-associated microbes in one month, and two of them are fungal.** Cancer Cell has the intratumoral mycobiome promoting lung cancer progression through myeloid-derived suppressor cells ([37738973](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37738973/)) and, separately, a named tumour-resident bacterium conferring chemoradiation resistance via a lactate-driven metabolic shift ([37863066](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37863066/)). Nature Immunology has fungal microbiota sustaining activation of neutrophils and their progenitors in severe COVID-19 ([37872315](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37872315/)) — the microbiome acting on host haematopoiesis rather than on local tissue. All three are causal mechanisms with a named organism and a named effector arm, which is what separates this month's microbiome evidence from the compositional-association literature it sits in.

**Engineered cell therapy moves on three axes at once.** Nature Medicine doses a CAR against a solid-tumour antigen in patients alongside an RNA vaccine that amplifies the product in vivo ([37872225](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37872225/)); Cell points engineered T cells at an autoantibody-defined B cell population in a neurological autoimmune disease ([37918394](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37918394/)); and Nature reports peptide-centric CARs against intracellular oncoproteins ([37938771](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37938771/)), with Immunity reaching the same class of target by a different route using dimeric IgA ([37909039](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37909039/)). Solid tumours, autoimmunity and the intracellular proteome are three distinct barriers, and the `cell-therapy` claim is precisely that the platform crosses them.

**A non-PD-1 checkpoint reaches a clinical readout, and TIM-3 is worked on twice.** Nature Medicine reports a phase 1 result for a molecule targeting both PD-1 and LAG-3 across solid and haematologic disease ([37857711](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37857711/)) — clinical-stage evidence the category mostly lacks, since most of its content is preclinical target nomination. On the nomination side, JITC puts a myeloid-restricted receptor forward as a checkpoint that improves anti-PD-1 in gastric cancer ([37935567](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37935567/)), and TIM-3 is attacked twice in two days by different groups and different modalities: antibody blockade in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma ([37802053](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37802053/)) and a small-molecule inhibitor ([37967204](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37967204/)).

**Interception's precursor layer gets measured in tissue and in blood.** Nature Genetics runs two papers in the same issue on mosaic chromosomal alterations — a pan-tissue survey ([37904053](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37904053/)) and a whole-genome analysis across ancestries in blood ([37904051](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37904051/)) — establishing the clonal precursor state as something with population-scale structure rather than case reports. Blood reports a circulating protein elevated years ahead of a Hodgkin lymphoma diagnosis ([37748137](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37748137/)), which makes the same window accessible without a tissue sample.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Science Immunology publishes two documented costs of removing a suppressive population, in the same month. Regulatory T cells are shown to shield muscle mitochondria from interferon-γ damage, which is how exercise produces its benefit ([37922340](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37922340/)); and CSF1R-dependent macrophages — the lineage most routinely nominated for depletion in tumours — turn out to be required for epithelial regeneration after radiation injury ([37922341](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37922341/)). The second is the more awkward for `suppressive-population-inversion`, because irradiated tissue is not a hypothetical setting: it is the tissue of the patients in whom myeloid depletion would be combined with radiotherapy. The thread's claim is that removing these populations improves antitumour outcomes; neither paper contradicts that directly, and both price it.

Two cell-therapy failure modes are created by the engineering rather than by the disease. Nature reports latent human herpesvirus 6 reactivating inside the manufactured T cell product itself ([37938768](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37938768/)). Nature Cancer reports acquired resistance to a T-cell engager against a new myeloma antigen through genetic or epigenetic inactivation of that target ([37653140](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37653140/)) — antigen escape following the platform to a fresh antigen rather than being a peculiarity of the one it started on.

JITC traces anti-PD-1 resistance in melanoma to a chromatin repressor acting inside the tumour cell on its own MHC class II ([38315170](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38315170/)), which is the tumour-intrinsic account `immunotherapy-resistance` claims is being displaced. And Immunity prints the neoantigen field's improvement and its limits together: machine learning with harmonised data raises immunogenicity prediction ([37816353](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37816353/)), and in the same issue an accompanying piece names the trade-offs the prediction step cannot escape ([37967528](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37967528/)). A journal contesting a claim within one issue is a better signal about the state of that claim than either paper alone.

### (b) Method credibility

Genome Biology reports that a gene family in wide use is misannotated at scale — DNA transposons catalogued as a general transcription factor ([37957683](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37957683/)). This is the worst kind of failure for `method-credibility`, because the error is in the reference rather than in a tool: anything that looked the gene up inherits it, and nothing in a downstream analysis would reveal it.

A chromatin mark is being redefined across two journals in six weeks. Nature described acetyl-methyllysine marking chromatin at active transcription start sites in October ([37731000](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37731000/)); Nature Genetics now reports it as a dual modification of histone H4 ([37938719](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37938719/)). When a mark's identity is in motion, so is every dataset that assayed it — though two papers refining one modification is the ordinary way a mark gets characterised, and it is worth less than the misannotation above, where the error is already in the reference.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This paragraph ran to three journals, the third being a Science piece titled
    *A case of mistaken epigenetic identity* ([37943909](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37943909/)), which was read as a
    reassignment of the mark across the published record. The title is a pun. The
    paper's entire abstract is one sentence — "The specialized packaging of sperm
    DNA preserves genome stability in the fruit fly zygote" — and it is not about
    acetyl-methyllysine, about reproducibility, or about the reference at all. Its
    card has been withdrawn and carries no thread. Nothing in this month's
    method-credibility column depends on it.

Nature Genetics also shows that discovery of genetic effects on gene expression and on complex traits is systematically non-overlapping ([37857933](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37857933/)), with a companion framing the same result as a power paradox ([37857936](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37857936/)) — the routine practice of reading gene function off association statistics is biased by the study design, not by the biology. And Science publishes prediction-powered inference ([37943906](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37943906/)), a correction procedure for drawing valid conclusions when model predictions stand in for measurements. It belongs here because of what its existence concedes: without it, treating model output as data is invalid, and a great deal of published work does exactly that.

### How to read the ratio

Eight of this month's twenty-two cards refute, and the quarter runs near forty per cent — above the corpus's established rate. That is a property of how these months were read, not of the months: the reading brief ranked refutations first and went looking for them. The reading was originally done against titles alone, so a stance was recorded only where the title stated it and papers that bury their conclusion were underrepresented regardless of quality. Those were recovered by an abstract re-scan on 2026-09-04. This month is the least title-hidden of 2023 — 25% against a year average of 59% — and it is also the month whose refutation share fell most on re-reading, from near forty per cent to eleven of forty. And it was done in arrears. Each card is written to what its title supports in November 2023, but that is a discipline applied by hand rather than something the method enforces.
